observations: Photo 0: Black Nikon DSLR held in hand, articulated LCD screen flipped out to the left, mode dial on right with P/S/A/M and scene modes, hot shoe visible, green indicator light near viewfinder.
Photo 1: Front-top angle of same camera with lens mounted; lens appears to be a standard zoom kit lens rather than a short prime lens.
Photo 2: Front angle, "Nikon" clearly readable on camera pentaprism, lens is a standard zoom with zoom ring, flip screen open to the right.

claims.evidence: Nikon brand readable in photo 2, but model number D5100 not visible in any photo
photo 2 shows a standard zoom kit lens, not a short 50mm prime
no Yongnuo branding visible on lens in any photo
condition cannot be confirmed remotely from photos alone

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or function (shutter, sensor, autofocus, LCD)
risks.proof: video of camera turning on, taking a photo, and reviewing the image

risks.risk: Shutter count unknown or high usage
risks.proof: screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or third-party tool

risks.risk: Lens has fungus, scratches, or aperture oil
risks.proof: close-up photos of front and rear lens glass and aperture blades

risks.risk: Battery and charger not included or not working
risks.proof: photo of battery and charger, or video of camera running on battery

risks.risk: Actual camera model is not D5100 (could be D5000 or other)
risks.proof: clear photo of model name on camera body

proof_requests: Clear photo of the camera model name on the body
Video of camera powering on, taking a shot, and displaying the image
Close-up of lens front and rear glass
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a used Nikon DSLR with a standard zoom lens; even with unproven functionality and a contradicted lens claim, it can be priced at its worst case as an untested Nikon DSLR body with kit lens.
